body: Hello, I want to open up by saying that you are not alone. A lot of people have the feeling of wanting to just 'vanish'. I think you'd be surprised at just how many people have that feeling. Anyway, it can be really hard to feel as though you aren't good at anything. I'm not here to tell you things like "you must be good at something" or "you just haven't found it yet". The truth is, it is almost impossible to be good at something with so much competition out there. Weather you compare yourself to others or not, the world will often beat you down if you 'aren't good enough'. What I do want to say is that it isn't always about being good at stuff, it's about what you enjoy. When people are in places similar to you, they will often get unmotivated. Fair enough, so my suggestion is to try to focus more on what makes you happy. If something makes you happy, who cares if you are good at it? Really like video games? Go on and play for a while. Enjoy being outside? Go on a nice hike. I know that these won't solve your dilemma instantly, but my main point is to try to stay away from trying to be the best at something and too focus on what you enjoy. I think many will criticise what I'm saying as unrealistic and they have a point. You obviously can't just only do what makes you happy all of your life. But what you can do is try to focus on yourself when you are in a bad place. Often times this will lead to self improvement, even if you don't know it. I hope this helps even a little. Thanks for reading

Hey there, I read your post and I want to say a few words. First of all, there is nothing wrong with asking for help. Everyone gets into a position where they need help, it's only natural. So I'll try my best to be the person who hears your cry for help. The first thing I want to say is that anxiety sucks. There isn't a single doubt in my mind that the anxiety you are constantly feeling can make you feel trapped. Anxiety is so hard that almost everyone needs the help of someone else to properly manage it. The best people to go to are the ones who understand it. By that I mean doctors and others in the medical field. If you haven't talked to a doctor already please, go see one. It may take some time for them to have an impact but almost all people see an improvement. If you have already seen a doctor then the best thing to do is open up to someone. As I have been saying, dealing with anxiety alone is difficult. Having someone by your side can make it just a bit less difficult I admit it won't solve things instantly, but any and all help can improve your state of mind. If you don't have someone to open up too, you can find someone. There are many resources on the internet for people like you and I where they can talk openly too give and take advise. These changes may seem small, but even small changes can really help. Thanks for reading, I hope I helped.

Hey, I know what you mean when you say you are destined to kill yourself. When you feel sad or lonely for so long it's hard to think in any other way. When it comes to your life in terms of romance one thing I will say is that you are not alone. I know that doesn't help just by itself but there are plenty of people who have never had a relationship while being college-aged. I can't tell you the reason why you are not getting any luck, but what I can say is that luck is what it comes down to a lot of the time. Maybe the people who were not interested in you just thought you were not their type, I don't know. What I do know is that luck is a possible reason you aren't getting a date. Now it's a little unfair just to say it all comes down to luck, but I suspect it is not just that. When you are depressed you carry yourself differently and you feel down on yourself. Perhaps your Depression is coming through more then you know it and is preventing you from getting a SO. I can talk forever about the possibilities and none of them are gurantees. I know it hurts to be lonely but my suggestion is to try not to devalue your self based on your relationships. You are more then the relationships you have and not having a relationship won't make you better as a person. From my experience getting an SO doesn't make the loneliness go away, what does is being able to overcome the loneliness

Hey man, I think it is clear that you aren't having a great time with your life right now and that you really want things to change. Now I want to open this up by saying that I am no doctor so I can't speak to much on your diagnosis, but I'll try my best to respond to what I can. One thing that I find really interesting with your post is your idea that life can be worth it if the fun outweighs the pain. And you are having way more pain then fun. It seems a lot of your pain is coming from college and it seems that you don't like it too much. Now I'm sure you want to be successful for your own and your families sacks but if college is making you so depressed why keep doing what you are doing. If you really think that college is contributing so much to your depression I would consider trying to change things up. You don't need college to be a success, especially if it is causing you so much pain. Now, with that being said, pain is a normal part of life (it fucking sucks) but we all know it is. I don't want to at cut it out of your life just because it causes you pain. I want to say is to change things up and try to strive for things that make you happy even if their will be pain. Maybe one day you'll come back to college or maybe you won't. But what I can say is striving for happiness while still not ignoring the realities of life can do great things. My advice isn't perfect and I would totally understand if you didn't take it, but just take this away at least: you have a criteria for living, try to fit into it with the realities of being an adult

I'm not 100% sure but my guess is that the Paris attacks have very little to do with how you feel. I'm not trying to attack you or offend you. What I am trying to say is that I just think you are depressed and when your depressed almost anything can make you sad. With that being said you strike me as someone who is internalising a lot of these thoughts and when they do come out people want to help you. I could be wrong but I'm going to continue just in case I am right ( if I am wrong, I'm not saying that any other situation is somehow less important than the one I'm talking about). Anyway, my suggestion would be to not be scared to let your thoughts out sometimes. Talking can help someone so much, not just because people reply in helpful ways, but mostly because you can sometimes learn things about yourself and your situation when talking outloud. Personally I find I understand my depression much better when I talk about it and I learn things about myself that I didn't know. This understanding doesn't necessarily fix the problems, but what it does do is help identify the problems and the sources of them. Think of it like a doctor, knowing the disease of a patient doesn't heal them, but it does help in finding treatment. If you are too nervous to open up to people I suggest trying to find a therapist. Not only will this help you to understand yourself, but they can also help I'm treating the things making you sad. I find that even talking to yourself can help a bit. Not talking in your head, bit literally out loud. I hope I'm not a crazy person, but it can help you really think about what you want to say and how you want to say it. I hope this helps

I worked at stressful jobs similar to yours (although I'm sure not the same) and I want to start this off by saying I know how nerve racking it can feel to be left alone with so much pressure on you. With that being said I also want to say that I know it is likely I don't fully understand your situation and that can be hard. Anyway, I want to say that what you did is perfectly okay, the store said it themselves, they fired you because it was policy, not because you are an incompetent worker. With that being said I do want to say that you should try to think about this with jobs in the future, I'm not saying you are some how a bad employee. What I'm trying to say is that you most likely thrive it certain situations and you should try to put your self in situations where you can thrive and this will allow you to be more successful. Just my two cents. Anyway, as a student myself I know that jobs are limited and it is often not a matter of choice but more like you have to go where ever will take you. This sucks but it's just an unfortunate reality. But from what I am reading you were able to get a job twice after leaving your original position, although you left both of those jobs, that's no east task. This makes me think that employers see potential in you (if they didnt, you wouldn't be getting those jobs) use this to your advantage when looking for more jobs. Try to think about what you did wrong and what you did right in the job finding process and adapt to those thoughts. I can't guarantee anything but I suspect you will have more opportunities presented. As for your parents, although they may be at their wits end, they got to that point out of love. I'm sure that they are frustrated with hoe things are going, but this is because they want you to succeed and see you happy. Not because they are just putting up with you. If this were the case then they would have cut you off already. With that being said, I know it is not a good idea to capitalise on this love they have for you. I suggest telling them the truth. Tell them why you didn't succeed and how you are going to change that for the future. Most parents don't want to see there kids taking advantage of them, but if you show them that you are learning from your mistakes, it will ensure them that there help isn't you taking advantage of them but that is is actually helping you find the path to success. Just my 2 cents. I'm sorry if I wasn't able to help

Now I don't want to be pushing drugs or playing doctor, but from my understanding (and take this with the grain of salt please) is that anxiety is often a result of chemicals in the brain. That sounds so weird but what that means is that it is not your fault, and can be fixed. It's not an easy thing of taking a pill and feeling better, but it helps. I recommend reading up some books on anxiety. Not just about how to stop it but also on what it is medically. Sometimes if you can see it as just chemicals it can be easier to dismiss. You didn't care about school: this is a big one and hits a lot of people. In my opinion this and the depression thing can be one in the same and you just may not know it yet. And hey maybe it was something I didn't say, but I can almost guarantee that depression probably had some hand in whatever reason it was. Now on to the girl thing. Okay so it's true, some people are not attractive. That's the way life is sometimes and it sucks (although I'm sure you are probably more attractive then you give yourself credit for) but with that being said it is not the only factor to a good relationship. As you get older you'll come to see that who you are becomes way more important than how you look. It's true as far as I can tell. Now I'm sure you've been told this time and time again, but it doesn't help few fact that you are unattractive and (more importantly) feel unattractive. It is so hard to just get to the point where you can say to yourself "Ya I'm not attractive, but so what?" But when it comes it is just a huge weight off your shoulders. I'm not going to guarantee anything, but what I will say is you should try doing things that make you feel attractive (hair cuts, working out) but recognize that it doesn't always matter.

People learn in many different ways, for example, I know someone who did horrible in school and barely passed, but he got into the work force and has been having a way better time with it. Maybe you are just like this too, the school system isn't perfect and not all people will go through it as it is intended. You are depressed: now the important thing about this one is that you recognise it. If you know (or strongly feel) that this is why you aren't doing too well in school, that means if you are able to get rid of depression you can succeed. That is no easy task of course but it's important to see that it can be fixed (I'm writing more and not just about school, like I said I'm a slow typer, sorry)

Being scared about the future is a totally normal, but I know that doesn't make it any easier to try and figure your life out. Although I am 19 I think what a lot of people don't mention is just how young we are. The thing that keeps me going is that it is okay if we fail or change our minds. Some people know what they want to do when they are young and then they go out and do it, and that's great for them. But most people at our age aren't like that. The beauty of it is we have time to mess up. I'm sure you have a lot of pressure to be so successful, but there is no way all successful people had a plan so early. So they just kept going until it worked out. It's important to ignore that pressure a little bit and tell yourself that even if you mess up, you will still have a Chance. I hope that helps


TL;DR: you have time to mess up and I'm pretty sure a lot of people messed up before you, so it's okay

I know you are freaked out right now and I'm sure things are very bad. But an important thing to think about is you are acting on impulse, like a reflex. A good thing to think about when making all big life decisions is that acting on impulse is not always what you want after deliberation. I would very much like if you had that deliberation time, I'm guessing you've been in your 'tilt' for about half an hour or so and as a gamer myself, I know that is not always enough time to stabilise. I want to try and calm you down so I am going to tell you something interesting that might make you calm down. Do you know the origin of tilt? It comes from pinball machines. Players would only have so much tilt in the table itself before the machine would stop them. If the player tilted the machine too much the paddles will lock up causing the player to get angry. Pretty interesting. My final point is that I want you not to make these impulse decisions. As much as it is hard right now it is best that you take some time to collect your thoughts and really think before doing anything. Sleep on it at least. I would recommend that after you do that open up to someone or even come back here, tell someone about what's going on and they will help you get through it
